description: Na₄Ca₂P₂SO₁₂ crystallizes in the monoclinic Cc space group. There are four inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.47-2.94 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.58-2.95 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.48-2.81 Å. In the fourth Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.51-2.78 Å. There are two inequivalent Ca sites. In the first Ca site, Ca is bonded to six O atoms to form CaO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent SO₄ tetrahedra and corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Ca-O bond distances ranging from 2.25-2.37 Å. In the second Ca site, Ca is bonded to six O atoms to form CaO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent SO₄ tetrahedra and corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Ca-O bond distances ranging from 2.23-2.41 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four CaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 29-42°. There are two shorter (1.55 Å) and two longer (1.56 Å) P-O bond lengths. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four CaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 31-42°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.55-1.57 Å. S is bonded to four O atoms to form SO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four CaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 29-39°. There are two shorter (1.49 Å) and two longer (1.50 Å) S-O bond lengths. There are twelve inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, and one P atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, and one S atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, and one P atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, and one S atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded to three Na, one Ca, and one P atom to form a mixture of distorted corner, edge, and face-sharing ONa₃CaP trigonal bipyramids. In the eighth O site, O is bonded to three Na, one Ca, and one P atom to form a mixture of distorted corner, edge, and face-sharing ONa₃CaP trigonal bipyramids. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Ca, and one S atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded to three Na, one Ca, and one P atom to form a mixture of distorted corner, edge, and face-sharing ONa₃CaP trigonal bipyramids. In the eleventh O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Ca, and one S atom. In the twelfth O site, O is bonded to three Na, one Ca, and one P atom to form a mixture of distorted corner, edge, and face-sharing ONa₃CaP trigonal bipyramids.
